entries.name: Rebel Cell Recruit
entries.summary:
A rebel, resistance, dissident, insurgent, separatist, or revolutionary group has approached you as a possible recruit, supporter, contact, or useful asset.

Narrative effects: Recruitment pressure has taught you about the faction involved and what it means to face a choice carrying political danger. This trait does not establish that you joined.

entries.name: Recent Exile
entries.summary:
You were recently forced or ordered away from your home, territory, organization, people, institution, or community.

Narrative effects: Exile has forced you to understand unfamiliar communities while finding routes through places that are not yet home.

entries.name: Rejected From the Path You Wanted
entries.summary:
You seriously pursued a profession, institution, relationship, appointment, guild, military post, education, or other future and were rejected.

Narrative effects: Rejection forced you to face disappointment while learning more about how opportunities are actually granted and denied.

entries.name: Reluctant Heir
entries.summary:
A title, estate, business, office, household position, inheritance, or other significant responsibility is expected to pass to you, and you are not certain you want it.

Narrative effects: Expectations of inheritance have made formal identity and the discipline required to carry unwanted responsibility difficult to ignore.

entries.name: Rent or Board Is Due
entries.summary:
Your next rent, room payment, board, lodging fee, or household contribution is due soon, and you do not currently have enough comfortable margin to ignore it.

Narrative effects: Immediate housing costs have made you practical about money and disciplined about what must be paid before anything else.

entries.name: Runaway Heir
entries.summary:
You left behind an inheritance, title, business, estate, formal household position, or other expected succession and have reasons not to advertise who you are.

Narrative effects: You understand the identity you fled and have learned how to keep parts of it concealed. This trait does not establish royal or special blood unless another story element does.

entries.name: Rebel Contact Adult
entries.summary:
You became a contact, helper, courier, sympathizer, lookout, or minor participant in rebel, reformist, outlaw, or dissident activity.

Narrative effects: You ask who benefits when authority calls someone a criminal.

entries.name: Relic Hunter Novice
entries.summary:
You began searching ruins, old battlefields, sealed vaults, forgotten shrines, or abandoned noble holdings for relics and valuables. Curiosity, greed, scholarship, debt, or desperation may have led you there.

Narrative effects: You treat old objects as questions with sharp edges.

entries.name: Road Courier
entries.summary:
You worked as a courier, messenger, road runner, mounted carrier, temple runner, faction contact, or delivery agent across distance.

Narrative effects: You think of distance in weather, road quality, danger, and how urgent the sealed message feels.

entries.name: Royal Attendant
entries.summary:
You served near royalty, high nobility, heirs, palace officials, royal guests, or protected bloodlines. You learned the ritual distance between service and danger.

Narrative effects: You know how close one can stand to power while still being expected to vanish into the room.

entries.name: Quiet Rule-Follower
entries.summary:
You usually followed rules without needing much supervision. Whether from caution, respect, habit, or a dislike of conflict, adults learned that you were rarely the child creating obvious trouble.

Narrative effects: You notice expected behavior quickly and find it easy to maintain composure when following established rules.

entries.name: Rebellious Child
entries.summary:
Rules invited questions, commands invited resistance, and adults who expected obedience often discovered you wanted an explanation first. Your childhood defiance could be admirable, exhausting, or both.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable challenging authority verbally and are less easily cowed by disapproval alone.

entries.name: Remembered Every Face
entries.summary:
You had an unusually strong memory for people. Visitors, neighbors, merchants, distant relatives, workers, teachers, and other children often remained recognizable long after brief meetings.

Narrative effects: People tend to remain distinct in your memory, especially when their expression or behavior made an impression.

entries.name: Remembered Every Route
entries.summary:
Once someone took you somewhere, you rarely forgot how to get back. Roads, turns, landmarks, bridges, stairs, alleys, and spatial relationships stayed unusually clear in your mind.

Narrative effects: You build reliable mental maps quickly and find it natural to translate remembered routes into spatial representations.

entries.name: River Swimmer
entries.summary:
Rivers, ponds, lakes, canals, or sheltered coastal water became part of your childhood play. Swimming was recreation, exploration, escape from heat, or simply another way to get somewhere.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable moving through water and thinking about currents, banks, landmarks, and reachable routes.

entries.name: Roof Runner
entries.summary:
Roofs, walls, sheds, balconies, fences, and raised walkways became part of your childhood playground. You learned quickly that the fastest route was not always the one built for walking.

Narrative effects: You naturally consider elevated, narrow, and unconventional routes when moving through built environments.

entries.name: Runaway for a Day
entries.summary:
Once, whether from anger, curiosity, fear, or stubborn independence, you left home and stayed away long enough for people to worry. You eventually returned or were found, but the memory stayed with you.

Narrative effects: Leaving familiar supervision and finding your own way through an environment does not feel entirely foreign.

entries.name: Quarry Child
entries.summary:
Stone faces, ramps, carts, wedges, cranes, dust, heavy blocks, workers, and the constant reshaping of the landscape surrounded your childhood.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with the practical systems used to move heavy stone and with the physical effort involved.

entries.name: Raised by Older Children
entries.summary:
Older siblings, cousins, street youths, wards, apprentices, or neighborhood children shaped much of your everyday life. Children taught you many of the rules adults assumed someone else was explaining.

Narrative effects: You understand informal peer hierarchies, games, favors, reputations, and the social rules children create among themselves.

entries.name: Remote Farm Child
entries.summary:
Your childhood home stood far from dense settlement. Long distances, isolated work, seasonal routines, limited visitors, and solving small problems without immediate outside help were normal.

Narrative effects: Solitude, routine, and ordinary environmental knowledge feel familiar rather than restrictive.

entries.name: Restricted Household Child
entries.summary:
Your childhood place within the household or community was shaped by strict controls over duties, movement, access, and permission. Adults or authorities determined much of what you could do and where you could go.

Narrative effects: You learned to control outward reactions and pay close attention to supervision, permissions, and visible changes in authority. This trait describes childhood rather than your present circumstances.

entries.name: Riverbank Explorer
entries.summary:
Riverbanks, bridges, reeds, shallows, islands, canals, docks, stepping stones, and changing water levels made up a large part of your childhood exploration.

Narrative effects: Moving around waterways feels familiar, and you naturally think about banks, crossings, currents, and reachable routes.

entries.name: Roadside Inn Child
entries.summary:
A roadside inn or stopping place became your childhood world. Drivers, wagons, couriers, traders, pilgrims, animals, weather reports, and road gossip arrived constantly.

Narrative effects: Road travelers are familiar company, and you understand both their vehicles and the information they carry from place to place.

entries.name: Reach Control Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in controlling space with long thrusting and pole weapons, combining spear precision with broader polearm concepts. Your training emphasizes denying approaches, managing multiple distances, and forcing enemies to cross dangerous ground before reaching you.

Narrative effects: You treat reach as territory, constantly judging which spaces an opponent can enter safely and which should cost them for every step.

entries.name: Quick Aim
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors agility, balance, speed, and bodily control, while aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Dexterity and +2 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with agility, balance, speed, and bodily control, calling on aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Quick Mind
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors agility, balance, speed, and bodily control, while memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Dexterity and +2 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with agility, balance, speed, and bodily control, calling on memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Quick Reasoning
entries.summary:
You combine agility, balance, speed, and bodily control with memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Dexterity and +4 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing agility, balance, speed, and bodily control and memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Quiet Conviction
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors inner resolve, supported by enough presence for your words and decisions to carry weight when you choose to speak. Grants +6 Willpower and +2 Communication.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure, calling on presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Ranged Discipline
entries.summary:
Your combat aptitude strongly favors aim and exact placement, while enough fighting instinct remains to manage pressure and close threats. Grants +6 Accuracy and +2 Fighting.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement, calling on close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Reactive Awareness
entries.summary:
You combine agility, balance, speed, and bodily control with awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Dexterity and +4 Perception.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing agility, balance, speed, and bodily control and awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Resolute Fighter
entries.summary:
You combine close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges with resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Fighting and +4 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges and resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Resolute Power
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure, while physical power, leverage, and force provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Willpower and +2 Strength.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure, calling on physical power, leverage, and force to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Resolute Strength
entries.summary:
You combine physical power, leverage, and force with resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Quarry Family
entries.summary:
Generations of your family cut, hauled, sorted, sold, or worked stone from quarries. Weight, fracture, quality, dangerous faces, useful blocks, waste, and the difference between valuable stone and ordinary rubble were practical family concerns.

Narrative effects: You understand the physical reality of stone work and have a practiced sense for the quality and usefulness of quarried material.

entries.name: Rebel Bloodline
entries.summary:
Your family has a repeated history of rebellion, resistance, political defiance, mutiny, forbidden organization, or ending up on the wrong side of established authority. Whether those causes were heroic, foolish, criminal, necessary, or different in every generation is another question.

Narrative effects: You understand why resistance movements hide meetings, test loyalty, fear informants, split into factions, and disagree over whether defiance is courage, necessity, or catastrophe. This legacy does not make you a rebel yourself.

entries.name: Roadborn Line
entries.summary:
Caravaners, couriers, guides, traders, teamsters, messengers, or other travelling workers recur throughout your family history. Routes, weather, inns, crossings, pack animals, bargains, and distant acquaintances became a kind of inherited geography.

Narrative effects: You think about distance through roads, stops, crossings, supplies, trustworthy hosts, and what can be traded when coin is not enough.

entries.name: Regional Lorekeeper
entries.summary:
You know regions as lived places: settlements, local customs, roads, rulers, old names, landmarks, neighboring peoples, recurring dangers, travel expectations, and the stories communities tell about themselves. Your knowledge may be broad or concentrated in places that matter to your background.

Narrative effects: You remember local names, customs, route habits, regional warnings, and the practical differences that disappear on a formal map.

entries.name: Relic Scholar
entries.summary:
You study enchanted objects, ancient weapons, heirlooms, sealed artifacts, cursed items, ceremonial objects, lost devices, and the histories attached to them. You know how provenance, construction, legend, and observed behavior can matter as much as an object's apparent value.

Narrative effects: You examine old objects through provenance, workmanship, recorded history, known reactions, and the possibility that the popular story about a relic is incomplete or wrong.

entries.name: Religious Scholar
entries.summary:
You have studied faiths, doctrines, sacred histories, rituals, institutions, taboos, holy places, theological disputes, saints, cults, and the social role of religion. Religious knowledge does not prove divine favor and does not grant Heroic Arcana or any other magic.

Narrative effects: You recognize doctrine, ritual context, sacred precedent, theological disagreements, and the historical reasons different communities may interpret the same religious act differently.

entries.name: Ritual Scholar
entries.summary:
You specialize in formal rituals where magical structure, symbolic action, sacred tradition, timing, preparation, witnesses, or prescribed procedure materially affect the result. You understand both arcane and religious frameworks without treating them as interchangeable, and this focus grants no ritual ability or magical access by itself.

Narrative effects: You look for sequence, symbols, preparation, participants, magical structure, sacred meaning, and the point where a ritual could fail because one framework was misunderstood.

entries.name: Rune Arcana
entries.summary: You have a natural gift for Rune Arcana: written magic, carved marks, spell diagrams, prepared inscriptions, ritual anchors, and power stabilized through symbols.

entries.name: Recognized Heir of Fenrisard-Argenwald
entries.summary:
The Crown has conclusively authenticated your descent from Roderan Fenrisard-Argenwald and recognized you as the lawful heir named by Othmar Fenrisard-Argenwald's final succession arrangements. Your identity and eligibility are no longer reasonably disputed under Crown law. This recognition does not mean you have accepted the inheritance, assumed its titles, taken possession of Varglund, claimed the Argent Seat, or been recognized as commander of the Runed Argent Fang.

Narrative effects: The Crown has conclusively authenticated the character as Roderan Fenrisard-Argenwald's lawful child and the recognized heir named by Othmar's succession arrangements. Crown officials, informed nobles, House Fenrisard-Argenwald members, and other knowledgeable NPCs should treat the character's identity and place in the succession as legally established rather than uncertain or mistaken. Hostile relatives may argue that the will was unjust, that the character is unfit, or that practical authority should pass elsewhere, but they should not repeatedly treat the bloodline as unproven without new and exceptional evidence. This trait establishes eligibility only. The character has not necessarily accepted the inheritance, received either Argent title, taken possession of the estate, activated the Argent Seat, or become First Fang.

entries.name: Relic Archaeologist
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Relic Lore and Searching as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Context Before Contact.

Narrative effects: Treat Relic Archaeologist as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Relic Lore with Searching when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Relic Lore skill 30, Searching skill 30

entries.name: Relic Channeler
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Relic Lore and Rune Arcana as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Borrowed Resonance.

Narrative effects: Treat Relic Channeler as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Relic Lore with Rune Arcana when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Relic Lore skill 30, Rune Arcana skill 30, Rune Arcana trait 1

entries.name: Relic Lore Apex
entries.summary:
Your command of relic lore is exceptional even among seasoned specialists. You combine economy, judgement, and control across provenance, artifact traditions, old enchantments, ownership history, warning signs, and judging what an ancient object may mean, while still respecting tools, resources, environment, and credible opposition.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an exceptional relic lore practitioner. Let expertise change what approaches are plausible, but never erase consequences, impossible geometry, unavailable tools, social authority, or established world rules.

entries.name: Relic Lore Discipline
entries.summary:
You have turned relic lore into a deliberate specialty through repeated practice. You are reliably trained in provenance, artifact traditions, old enchantments, ownership history, warning signs, and judging what an ancient object may mean, but difficult situations still depend on position, tools, opposition, and judgement.

Narrative effects: Treat relic lore as a practiced specialization. The character deliberately applies provenance, artifact traditions, old enchantments, ownership history, warning signs, and judging what an ancient object may mean; give that training weight without granting automatic success or ignoring normal constraints.

entries.name: Relic Lore Expertise
entries.summary:
Your relic lore remains reliable when conditions become complicated. You can adapt provenance, artifact traditions, old enchantments, ownership history, warning signs, and judging what an ancient object may mean to pressure, poor timing, difficult terrain, and active opposition instead of relying on ideal circumstances.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an experienced relic lore specialist who adapts technique under pressure. Preserve normal risk, resource costs, physical limits, law, witnesses, and opposition.

entries.name: Relic Lore Mastery
entries.summary:
Relic Lore has become one of your defining masteries. You recognize advanced openings and methods within provenance, artifact traditions, old enchantments, ownership history, warning signs, and judging what an ancient object may mean, and this trait grants the signature ability Wake the Provenance.

Narrative effects: Treat relic lore as a defining mastery. The character may use Wake the Provenance when its fictional setup is plausible; it creates a special option, not guaranteed success or permission to bypass unrelated skills.

entries.name: Riding Apex
entries.summary:
Your command of riding is exceptional even among seasoned specialists. You combine economy, judgement, and control across seat, reins, balance, mount communication, difficult terrain, and keeping control when speed or fear rises, while still respecting tools, resources, environment, and credible opposition.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an exceptional riding practitioner. Let expertise change what approaches are plausible, but never erase consequences, impossible geometry, unavailable tools, social authority, or established world rules.

entries.name: Riding Discipline
entries.summary:
You have turned riding into a deliberate specialty through repeated practice. You are reliably trained in seat, reins, balance, mount communication, difficult terrain, and keeping control when speed or fear rises, but difficult situations still depend on position, tools, opposition, and judgement.

Narrative effects: Treat riding as a practiced specialization. The character deliberately applies seat, reins, balance, mount communication, difficult terrain, and keeping control when speed or fear rises; give that training weight without granting automatic success or ignoring normal constraints.

entries.name: Riding Expertise
entries.summary:
Your riding remains reliable when conditions become complicated. You can adapt seat, reins, balance, mount communication, difficult terrain, and keeping control when speed or fear rises to pressure, poor timing, difficult terrain, and active opposition instead of relying on ideal circumstances.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an experienced riding specialist who adapts technique under pressure. Preserve normal risk, resource costs, physical limits, law, witnesses, and opposition.

entries.name: Riding Mastery
entries.summary:
Riding has become one of your defining masteries. You recognize advanced openings and methods within seat, reins, balance, mount communication, difficult terrain, and keeping control when speed or fear rises, and this trait grants the signature ability Emergency Dismount.

Narrative effects: Treat riding as a defining mastery. The character may use Emergency Dismount when its fictional setup is plausible; it creates a special option, not guaranteed success or permission to bypass unrelated skills.

entries.name: Roderan's Argent Lessons
entries.summary:
Before his death, Roderan taught the character a practiced sequence of touch, controlled breathing, balance, and measured mana channeling. He presented the lessons as practical exercises and never explained that they were foundational techniques of House Fenrisard-Argenwald.

Narrative effects: This trait represents training received and practiced while Roderan was alive, not a newly awakened bloodline power. The lessons grant Argent Measure but do not provide an Arcana, noble authority, weapon mastery, historical knowledge, or automatic control over enchanted objects.

entries.name: Royal Blood Privately Confirmed
entries.summary:
Trusted evidence has privately confirmed your royal connection to a limited circle, but the wider realm does not yet know or accept it. This may bring sealed counsel, hidden protection, political delay, dangerous secrecy, and powerful people deciding whether the truth should be revealed, buried, exploited, or protected.

Narrative effects: A truth known by too few people can still control too many choices.

facts.label: Excluded by
facts.value: Royal Origin Unproven, Royal Blood Suspected, Royal Blood Under Verification, Royal Blood Publicly Disputed, Royal Blood Publicly Recognized

entries.name: Royal Blood Publicly Disputed
entries.summary:
Your possible royal origin has become publicly known or politically exposed, but it is disputed, doubted, weaponized, or not yet lawfully recognized. Court factions, nobles, temples, rebels, foreign powers, and rumor networks may try to prove, control, exploit, or discredit the claim.

Narrative effects: Once the realm hears the claim, truth becomes only one part of the struggle.

facts.label: Excluded by
facts.value: Royal Origin Unproven, Royal Blood Suspected, Royal Blood Under Verification, Royal Blood Privately Confirmed, Royal Blood Publicly Recognized

entries.name: Royal Blood Publicly Recognized
entries.summary:
Your royal origin has been publicly recognized through sufficient evidence, witnesses, ritual context, royal confirmation, or formal authority. This changes your political position, but it does not erase succession law, remove existing royal family members, or grant uncontested power without further story development.

Narrative effects: Recognition answers one question and creates several more.

facts.label: Excluded by
facts.value: Royal Origin Unproven, Royal Blood Suspected, Royal Blood Under Verification, Royal Blood Privately Confirmed, Royal Blood Publicly Disputed

entries.name: Royal Blood Suspected
entries.summary:
Credible people, records, agents, witnesses, or faction observers suspect that your bloodline may matter to Valenreach's royal history. This is suspicion, not proof. The claim may bring cautious protection, surveillance, noble interest, sealed invitations, frightened witnesses, or competing interpretations.

Narrative effects: Uncertainty becomes dangerous once important people start treating it as possible.

facts.label: Excluded by
facts.value: Royal Origin Unproven, Royal Blood Under Verification, Royal Blood Privately Confirmed, Royal Blood Publicly Disputed, Royal Blood Publicly Recognized

entries.name: Royal Blood Under Verification
entries.summary:
Your possible royal connection is being actively tested, investigated, or compared against records, witnesses, bloodline signs, relic reactions, ritual procedures, or trusted testimony. Protection, caution, scrutiny, and political maneuvering may all surround the process.

Narrative effects: Protection and containment begin to look dangerously similar.

facts.label: Excluded by
facts.value: Royal Origin Unproven, Royal Blood Suspected, Royal Blood Privately Confirmed, Royal Blood Publicly Disputed, Royal Blood Publicly Recognized

entries.name: Royal Origin Unproven
entries.summary:
A possible royal connection has been raised, but it remains unproven. Evidence is incomplete, witnesses may be uncertain, and no institution has formally accepted the claim. The question itself may still draw attention from people who want to prove it, disprove it, hide it, or use it.

Narrative effects: A question has been spoken aloud, and it cannot be made harmless again.

facts.label: Excluded by
facts.value: Royal Blood Suspected, Royal Blood Under Verification, Royal Blood Privately Confirmed, Royal Blood Publicly Disputed, Royal Blood Publicly Recognized

entries.name: Ruin Arcana
entries.summary:
You carry a legendary resonance with Ruin Arcana, awakened only through a major story gate, explicit start rule, or manually authored consequence. Ruin Arcana governs collapse, endings, broken structures, failing magic, decay of order, doomed patterns, and the moment when something can no longer remain whole. It should feel catastrophic, precise, and frightening even when used for a necessary purpose.

Narrative effects: You notice cracks, failing supports, doomed plans, brittle pride, and the point where one strike could bring everything down.

entries.name: Ruin Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Ruin Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Name the Weak Point.

Narrative effects: Treat Ruin Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Ruin Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Name the Weak Point when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Ruin Surveyor
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Cartography and Searching as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Safe Survey Line.

Narrative effects: Treat Ruin Surveyor as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Cartography with Searching when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

entries.name: Rune Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Rune Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Runic Cascade.

Narrative effects: Treat Rune Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Rune Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Runic Cascade when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Rune Enchanter
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Rune Arcana and Enchantment Arcana as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Bound Instruction.

Narrative effects: Treat Rune Enchanter as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Rune Arcana with Enchantment Arcana when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Rune Arcana skill 30, Enchantment Arcana skill 30, Rune Arcana trait 1, Enchantment Arcana trait 1

entries.name: Rune Engineer
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Rune Arcana and Engineering as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Runic Override.

Narrative effects: Treat Rune Engineer as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Rune Arcana with Engineering when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Rune Arcana skill 30, Engineering skill 30, Rune Arcana trait 1

entries.name: Running Apex
entries.summary:
Your command of running is exceptional even among seasoned specialists. You combine economy, judgement, and control across pace, breath, sprint timing, pursuit, escape, and preserving enough reserve for the decisive stretch, while still respecting tools, resources, environment, and credible opposition.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an exceptional running practitioner. Let expertise change what approaches are plausible, but never erase consequences, impossible geometry, unavailable tools, social authority, or established world rules.

entries.name: Running Discipline
entries.summary:
You have turned running into a deliberate specialty through repeated practice. You are reliably trained in pace, breath, sprint timing, pursuit, escape, and preserving enough reserve for the decisive stretch, but difficult situations still depend on position, tools, opposition, and judgement.

Narrative effects: Treat running as a practiced specialization. The character deliberately applies pace, breath, sprint timing, pursuit, escape, and preserving enough reserve for the decisive stretch; give that training weight without granting automatic success or ignoring normal constraints.

entries.name: Running Expertise
entries.summary:
Your running remains reliable when conditions become complicated. You can adapt pace, breath, sprint timing, pursuit, escape, and preserving enough reserve for the decisive stretch to pressure, poor timing, difficult terrain, and active opposition instead of relying on ideal circumstances.

Narrative effects: Treat the character as an experienced running specialist who adapts technique under pressure. Preserve normal risk, resource costs, physical limits, law, witnesses, and opposition.

entries.name: Running Mastery
entries.summary:
Running has become one of your defining masteries. You recognize advanced openings and methods within pace, breath, sprint timing, pursuit, escape, and preserving enough reserve for the decisive stretch, and this trait grants the signature ability Reserve Sprint.

Narrative effects: Treat running as a defining mastery. The character may use Reserve Sprint when its fictional setup is plausible; it creates a special option, not guaranteed success or permission to bypass unrelated skills.

entries.name: Rider
entries.summary:
You are highly practiced at controlling mounts during ordinary travel and difficult movement. Balance, reins, posture, terrain, animal mood, and the rider's own body all matter to how safely and efficiently a mount moves.

Narrative effects: You notice how a mount carries its weight, responds to pressure, and reacts to terrain before asking more from it.

entries.name: Route Finder
entries.summary:
You specialize in identifying a viable way through difficult or unfamiliar places: blocked roads, ruins, caves, dense settlements, broken terrain, river crossings, mountain approaches, and other spaces where the obvious path may fail.

Narrative effects: You look for continuity: where people, animals, water, carts, or old construction could realistically have passed.

entries.name: Quarry Sorter
entries.summary:
You sorted stone, moved smaller pieces, separated usable material from waste, and helped organize what more experienced workers extracted.

Narrative effects: You developed an eye for useful stone and familiarity with physically handling heavy material.

entries.name: Relic Room Sweeper
entries.summary:
You helped maintain a room, shrine, archive, treasury, or chamber containing old sacred or historical objects and learned that even dusty artifacts could carry meaning and value.

Narrative effects: Old objects invite you to consider both their significance and their physical quality.

entries.name: Ran Away Overnight
entries.summary:
You deliberately stayed away from home overnight after leaving through anger, curiosity, fear, rebellion, or a need to prove you could.

Narrative effects: Finding your own way without ordinary supervision became a real experience rather than childhood fantasy.

entries.name: Ran Messages for Rebels
entries.summary:
For a time, you carried messages, supplies, or simple instructions for rebels, dissidents, resistance members, insurgents, or another faction acting against local authority. You may or may not have understood their full cause.

Narrative effects: You learned how covert factions rely on routes and messengers. This trait does not require continued loyalty to the group.

entries.name: Reconciled With a Rival
entries.summary:
Someone who had been a rival, enemy, bully, competitor, or persistent source of conflict eventually became someone you could speak with, respect, or even befriend.

Narrative effects: You have personal experience turning hostility into workable understanding through conversation and perspective.

entries.name: Refused an Adult's Order
entries.summary:
You deliberately refused an adult's direct order because you believed obeying would be wrong, dangerous, humiliating, unfair, or simply unacceptable.

Narrative effects: You learned that refusing authority requires both nerve and the ability to explain why you will not comply.

entries.name: Runecrafter
entries.summary:
You are professionally trained in precise rune construction, inscription, material preparation, alignment, repair, and the magical principles required for functional runework. This training includes a minimal functional awakening of Rune Arcana, enough to unlock the Arcana and practice the craft without implying developed mastery.

Narrative effects: You inspect line, spacing, substrate, sequence, damage, and magical stability before trusting a rune. Your Rune Arcana access is real but may still be rudimentary.

facts.label: Modifiers
facts.value: Fine Script +15, Arcane Lore +5, Rune Arcana +1

entries.name: Rabbitfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Rabbitfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus long rabbit ears, expressive posture, quick movement, and compact athletic build. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Long ears, quick acceleration, responsive balance, and alert hearing favor rapid movement and reactions. Nervousness and timidity are not mandatory personality traits.

entries.name: Raccoonfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Raccoonfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus raccoon ears, a ringed tail, mask-like markings, quick fingers, and alert posture. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Sensitive hands, quick fingers, sharp close attention, and strong tactile awareness favor searching and delicate manipulation. Theft, scavenging, and criminality are not inherent racial behaviors.

entries.name: Ratfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Ratfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus rat ears or tail, quick hands, alert posture, and sharp senses. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Strong tolerance, scent awareness, and quiet movement help ratfolk function in difficult or crowded environments. Ratfolk ancestry does not make the character cowardly, criminal, unclean, or disease-ridden.

entries.name: Ravenfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Ravenfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus dark featherlike hair or markings, raven-dark eyes, possible winglike clothing patterns, and quick expressive movement. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Sharp sight and hearing support close observation and noticing changed details. Omens, cleverness, empathy, and mystical interpretation may exist in culture or personality but are not imposed by ancestry.

entries.name: Rumormonger
entries.summary:
You are skilled at gathering, tracing, testing, shaping, and deliberately circulating rumors through social networks. You understand that gossip changes as it moves, and you pay attention to who repeats a story, who benefits from it, and which version people are willing to believe.

Narrative effects: You remember where a story started, where it changed, and which version someone seems unusually eager to spread.

entries.name: Raincloak Travel Set
entries.summary: Travel clothing centered on a sturdy raincloak, suited for wet roads, storms, muddy villages, river crossings, and miserable weather.

entries.name: Ranger's Garb Set
entries.summary: Practical outdoor clothing suited for scouts, hunters, border runners, forest paths, and long travel through wild terrain.

entries.name: Refugee Rags Set
entries.summary: Worn, patched, mismatched clothing kept together by necessity. It suggests flight, loss, poverty, or survival after everything better was left behind.

entries.name: Reinforced Travel Gear Set
entries.summary: Durable travel gear reinforced with tough stitching, thicker layers, bracers, gloves, and practical protection. It is not proper armor, but it helps a traveler survive rough roads and sudden trouble.

entries.name: Quarterstaff
entries.summary: A sturdy two-handed staff useful for travel, defense, balance, and disciplined combat. Favored by monks, travelers, villagers, temple students, and mages who prefer a practical implement over a blade.

entries.name: Rapier
entries.summary: A slender thrusting blade suited for precision, dueling, courtly defense, and elegant violence. Favored by nobles, duelists, agents, and anyone who prefers timing over brute force.

entries.name: Recurve Bow
entries.summary: A compact, recurved bow suited for hunting, scouting, mounted use, and mobile skirmishing. It offers stronger draw and better range than a simple shortbow while remaining easier to carry and handle than a full longbow.

entries.name: Repeating Crossbow
entries.summary: A mechanism-fed crossbow that trades raw impact for faster follow-up shots and sustained pressure.

entries.name: Round Shield
entries.summary: A practical round shield used by warriors, guards, hunters, raiders, and frontier fighters. Balanced between defense, movement, and shield-bash utility.

entries.name: Rare Arcana Rumor
entries.summary:
A rumor spread that you possessed, might possess, or had shown signs of an unusual Arcana. Whether anyone was correct is not established by this trait.

Narrative effects: You became familiar with how magical rumors spread and how people interpret supposed signs of rare power. Do not treat the rumor as proof of an Arcana.

entries.name: Rebel Courier
entries.summary:
You carried messages, supplies, instructions, or information for rebels, dissidents, insurgents, resistance members, or another faction opposing authority.

Narrative effects: You learned how covert factions depend on routes, information, and trusted messengers. This does not require continued allegiance.

entries.name: Refused Recruitment
entries.summary:
A military, faction, gang, temple, guild, political group, or other organization tried to recruit you and you deliberately refused.

Narrative effects: Refusal taught you something about the organization that wanted you and about standing firm when another group expects compliance.

entries.name: Rejected Below Your Station
entries.summary:
Your interest in someone of lower status was rejected, discouraged, mocked, or made socially difficult because of the difference between you.

Narrative effects: The experience taught you that status can distort relationships even when the higher-status person believes it should not matter.

entries.name: Rumor Followed You
entries.summary:
A persistent rumor about your behavior, family, relationships, abilities, motives, or past followed you through part of your teenage life.

Narrative effects: Living under rumor taught you both how stories are maintained and how they affect the people being discussed. The rumor need not be true.

entries.name: Runaway Teen
entries.summary:
You deliberately left home, school, service, custody, an institution, or another expected place and attempted to remain away rather than returning after a brief absence.

Narrative effects: You learned to find your own routes and avoid being easily located without assuming that your escape happened in wilderness.

entries.name: Ranger Trainee
entries.summary:
You trained for work that demanded mobility, ranged fighting, fieldcraft, and the ability to defend yourself when an enemy closed the distance.

Narrative effects: Archery became your main martial foundation, with a light sidearm style for close encounters.

entries.name: Rejected by the Academy
entries.summary:
You prepared for formal education and attempted to gain entry to an academy, college, magical school, guild school, or similar institution, but were not accepted.

Narrative effects: Preparing for admission still gave you substantial academic practice and experience applying yourself toward demanding standards.

entries.name: Relic Curious
entries.summary:
Old objects fascinated you throughout adolescence. You studied relics, heirlooms, ruins, antiquities, ceremonial objects, recovered artifacts, and the clues that separated genuine history from attractive junk.

Narrative effects: You developed meaningful knowledge of relics alongside a practical eye for authenticity, workmanship, and material value.

entries.name: Quietly Adopted
entries.summary:
You were adopted while still very young without the event becoming a public spectacle or defining your whole childhood. The household that took you in simply became home, whether you later knew the details or not.

Narrative effects: You understand that belonging can be created through ordinary care, while questions about origins may still require asking rather than assuming.

entries.name: Raised Above an Inn
entries.summary:
Your earliest home sat above or beside an inn, tavern, boarding house, or similar public lodging. Voices, arguments, songs, travelers, rumors, footsteps, and late-night arrivals were ordinary background noise.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable learning about people through conversation and picking useful information out of busy social noise.

entries.name: Raised Behind a Shop
entries.summary:
Your toddler years unfolded behind, above, or beside a working shop. Customers, stock, coins, damaged goods, deliveries, prices, and the difference between valuable and worthless objects entered your world early.

Narrative effects: You instinctively notice the condition and value of ordinary goods and understand that nearly everything in a shop exists within an exchange.

entries.name: Raised Under Another Name
entries.summary:
During your earliest years, the name used for you was not necessarily the name attached to your birth, ancestry, or first household. The change may have been protective, practical, adoptive, fraudulent, cultural, or simply unexplained to you.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable with the idea that names can conceal, protect, simplify, or distort a person's history. This trait does not define why the name changed unless another part of the character history does.

entries.name: Raised by a Grandparent
entries.summary:
A grandparent or similarly older relative was one of your main caregivers during your first years. Family stories, old habits, inherited routines, and the perspective of another generation entered your life early.

Narrative effects: You grew up hearing the past discussed as lived memory rather than distant history and are sensitive to the needs and habits of older people.

entries.name: Raised in Shared Rooms
entries.summary:
Your earliest years were spent in crowded rooms, shared beds, servant quarters, orphan halls, communal homes, or cramped shelters. Privacy was rare, and learning to live around others came before independence.

Narrative effects: You are used to little privacy and can sleep through other people's noise.

entries.name: Raised in a Crowded Home
entries.summary:
You grew up surrounded by siblings, cousins, neighbors, other wards, or many adults under one roof. Noise, sharing, arguments, and constant company shaped your first understanding of home.

Narrative effects: You unconsciously make room for others even when space is scarce.

entries.name: Raised in a Farmhouse
entries.summary:
You spent your toddler years in a working farmhouse where livestock, fields, barns, feed, mud, weather, and the changing seasons were never far from the door.

Narrative effects: Working animals and ordinary rural environmental conditions feel familiar rather than exotic.

entries.name: Raised in a Guardhouse
entries.summary:
Your earliest years were spent around a guardhouse, watch post, gate station, or similar place where people came and went under observation. Watches, uniforms, weapons, visitors, alarms, and changing shifts were familiar sights.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to entrances, visible routines, uniforms, watch patterns, and signs that a guarded place has changed its posture.

entries.name: Raised in a Workshop
entries.summary:
Your first years were spent in or beside a working workshop where tools, materials, repairs, heat, texture, dust, scraps, and half-finished objects surrounded daily life.

Narrative effects: You have broad familiarity with physical materials and instinctively inspect texture, fit, wear, and construction through touch.

entries.name: Raised on a Barge
entries.summary:
A barge, riverboat, or similar working watercraft served as home during much of your toddlerhood. Rivers, docks, towpaths, currents, cargo, and repeated crossings formed the backdrop of your earliest years.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable thinking of waterways as routes and vessels as working homes rather than exotic transportation.

entries.name: Quiet Observer
entries.summary:
You spent long stretches simply watching people, objects, animals, and activity around you. Adults sometimes forgot you were paying attention until you reacted to something they thought you had missed.

Narrative effects: You naturally watch before acting and often notice both visible details and changes in people's expressions.

entries.name: Reached for Books
entries.summary:
Books, papers, tablets, illustrated pages, writing desks, and people reading attracted you long before you understood what the marks meant.

Narrative effects: Written material feels inviting rather than intimidating, though this temperament does not make you a scholar by itself.

entries.name: Quiet Movement Practice
entries.summary:
You trained to control weight, breathing, clothing, foot placement, and unnecessary motion so that moving carefully becomes almost automatic. Grants +2 Dexterity and +1 Perception.

Narrative effects: You notice loose boards, noisy gear, brushing fabric, unstable debris, and other small things that can betray movement.

entries.name: Recovery Discipline
entries.summary:
You trained around fatigue, minor injury, sleep loss, soreness, and physical recovery, learning how to judge your limits and return to useful condition efficiently. Grants +2 Constitution and +1 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to hydration, rest, pain, swelling, breathing, and other practical signs that tell you when to push and when recovery will matter more.

entries.name: Quarry Settlement
entries.summary:
You were raised near an open quarry or stoneworking settlement where extracting, splitting, moving, shaping, and supporting enormous amounts of stone required both physical labor and careful planning.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with moving heavy materials and understanding the constructed cuts, supports, ramps, and systems needed for large-scale stone work.

entries.name: Refugee Camp
entries.summary:
Displacement defined part of your upbringing. You lived among people who had left homes behind because of war, disaster, persecution, political upheaval, famine, occupation, magical danger, or another crisis.

Narrative effects: You understand displaced communities and are familiar with routes, origins, destinations, border movement, and the practical importance of knowing where people can go next.

entries.name: Restricted Household
entries.summary:
You were raised in a household or community where daily life was tightly controlled by an institution, employer, creditor, occupying power, or other authority. Work, movement, permissions, and expectations followed rules you and your caregivers had limited power to change.

Narrative effects: Living under strict authority taught you to control outward reactions and pay close attention to visible routines, supervision, and changes around you. This trait establishes upbringing rather than your present circumstances.

entries.name: Riverfolk Barges
entries.summary:
You grew up around barges, riverboats, towpaths, docks, currents, crossings, waterside trade, and communities whose homes and livelihoods followed navigable rivers.

Narrative effects: You understand directing watercraft and plotting routes through waterways without assuming experience with ocean sailing.

entries.name: Roadside Inn
entries.summary:
You grew up at an inn or stopping place along a significant road where wagons, coaches, carts, animals, traders, couriers, pilgrims, weather, road conditions, and travelers regularly arrived at the door.

Narrative effects: You gained familiarity with road vehicles and with extracting useful information from the steady flow of travelers.

entries.name: Rural Village
entries.summary:
You grew up in a small agricultural or country settlement where seasons, fields, nearby wilderness, local households, village disputes, marriages, favors, and gossip connected most people to one another.

Narrative effects: You understand the surrounding natural environment and how information moves through a small community.
